issues.subject: October at the shop: The Unlit Landing
issues.text:
The Slow Shelf · {date}

October at the shop: The Unlit Landing

The front table goes over to short novels this month. There are three to look at in the shop now, and Maud Sellick is coming in the week of 19 October.

The Unlit Landing, Maud Sellick
A woman takes a job clearing a small block of flats and makes the mistake of reading the notes pushed under a door. One hundred and twenty-eight pages, with a chapter set entirely on a bus that our Saturday bookseller read twice. The local library catalogue lists six copies across its branches. Our paperback is £9.50. Maud will read from the bus chapter here on Thursday 22 October at 19:00.
https://slowshelf.example/books/the-unlit-landing

Something for the Tuesday groups
Miriam Ash's The View from the Laundrette follows a street through one wash cycle at a time. The people who leave notes in the change bowl are more interesting than the person who keeps reading them. It's a good one to pass around if your group has a busy month coming. We have eight copies left from a carton with some battered corners, so those are £7 at the till.
https://slowshelf.example/reading-groups/october-paperbacks

The winter swap shelf
We'll put the swap crate beside the umbrella stand from Monday 19 October. Take a book or leave one, with a pencil note inside about where you stopped reading if you like. Please keep to two books per visit. Last winter someone left an entire box of gardening manuals, which was generous and meant we spent six weeks finding people with hedges.
https://slowshelf.example/shop/winter-swap-shelf

From behind the till,
Joanie Pritchard, bookseller

The Slow Shelf · 19 Harcombe Yard, Stoke Newington, London N16 0LS

issues.subject: September at the shop: books to read on the bus
issues.text:
The Slow Shelf · {date}

September at the shop: books to read on the bus

The back room seats are up again after the stocktake. We're using them for a reading that lasts half an hour, which is about the time it takes to get here on the 73.

Near the Front, Hettie Ransom
Ransom's debut is a collection of encounters in the same pair of bus seats. The driver knows most of the passengers by what they carry, and one chapter consists of the things left in the luggage space in a single week. It starts out rather funny. By the time a long-absent passenger returns with her folding shopping trolley, you'll know exactly what a big event that is.
https://slowshelf.example/books/near-the-front

Half an hour in the back room
Nora Belen and Hettie Ransom have chosen ten minutes each from their new books, followed by a few questions from the shop floor. The chairs are folding ones and we've taken out the middle row to keep a wider way through. Tickets are free. There's a line on the booking page to tell us if you want a chair with arms or space beside someone.
https://slowshelf.example/events/short-readings-september

Restarting a reading group
One local group is meeting at lunchtime now and needed books that could survive forty minutes of conversation. We sent them home with The Glass Bin, a novel told through the minutes of a residents' meeting. Read as far as the amendment about bicycles if you only have a night. The group loan box is back by the till and we'll hold up to six copies for a named organiser.
https://slowshelf.example/reading-groups/first-session-back

From behind the till,
Joanie Pritchard, bookseller

The Slow Shelf · 19 Harcombe Yard, Stoke Newington, London N16 0LS

issues.subject: August at the shop: the allotment books
issues.text:
The Slow Shelf · {date}

August at the shop: the allotment books

The shop door was open all last Saturday and the notes from the allotment got passed back and forth across the till. There are a few copies left and a tiny exhibition growing on the back wall.

The Seed Cupboard, Eric Haines
Haines spent a year drawing the packets in his aunt's seed cupboard, down to the date stamped on the lid of a tobacco tin. The essay at the end lets the aunt have a word too. Her account of why she kept that tin is worth the price of the pamphlet. Ours is the stitched second printing, with a bigger drawing of the hand-painted sign on the gate.
https://slowshelf.example/books/the-seed-cupboard

Ledger on the wall
The plot holders lent us a ledger with measurements written in the margins and a pressed bean leaf between two pages. We have it open to the month when the committee tried to agree how wide a path should be. The ink is faint on the right-hand page, so there is a larger printed copy on the wall that you can read from the bench.
https://slowshelf.example/events/ledger-of-the-plots

The reading group returns in September
We're starting again with Della Moss's When the Soil Moved, a novella about the woman sent to measure a road through a row of gardens. Moss spends almost a whole chapter on the first length of chalk line. It's only 144 pages, and we have a clean second-hand copy on the counter if you want to see how far the dialogue will carry you.
https://slowshelf.example/reading-groups/when-the-soil-moved

From behind the till,
Joanie Pritchard, bookseller

The Slow Shelf · 19 Harcombe Yard, Stoke Newington, London N16 0LS
